prompt: Show that the SI base units of the watt (W) are kg m^2 s^-3.

mark_scheme.criterion: Relates watt to joules and seconds (W = J s^-1) and expresses joule in base units as kg m^2 s^-2 (from W = Fs and F = ma).
Divides kg m^2 s^-2 by s to conclude with kg m^2 s^-3.

hints: Start with the definition P = W / t, so [P] = [W] / [t].
Express work in base units using W = Fs and F = ma.
solution: Power = work / time, so 1 W = 1 J s^-1. Work = force * distance = (kg m s^-2) * m = kg m^2 s^-2. Dividing by seconds gives (kg m^2 s^-2) / s = kg m^2 s^-3.
teacher_walkthrough: Award C1 for showing the base units of the joule: 1 J = 1 N m = 1 kg m^2 s^-2.
Award A1 for dividing by s to obtain kg m^2 s^-3.
